case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers Bluetooth SIG product registration using an existing qualified Bluetooth architecture and the completion of the registration process through submission, compliance-folder creation, and final delivery. The discussion includes qualification strategy validation, QDID selection under the post-July-2024 registration system, reuse of existing qualification assets, and future derivative-product registration. The consultant guided the customer through review-page approval, registration completion, compliance documentation collection, and post-registration obligations. The thread concludes with delivery of the compliance folder and instructions for future product additions.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A key qualification issue involved replacing legacy Subset-ID-based references because the newer Bluetooth SIG registration system no longer allows direct use of certain old Subset IDs. The consultant identified an alternative registration path by referencing existing qualified Link Layer and Host Layer QDIDs while retaining the desired PHY Layer implementation, allowing the intended registration to proceed. The consultant also verified that the selected qualification approach fit an Option 2b registration path and did not trigger additional test-plan requirements. The discussion further clarified that products using the same Bluetooth module and host stack can later be added as derivative products through Product List updates without requiring a new full registration.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is based on maximizing reuse of existing qualified Bluetooth designs while complying with current Bluetooth SIG registration rules. When legacy qualification references are no longer eligible under updated registration-system requirements, an equivalent qualified QDID combination should be identified that accurately represents the implemented architecture. If the resulting design remains within an approved qualification path and does not introduce additional test-plan obligations, registration can proceed without new testing. Future derivative products can leverage the same qualified architecture when the Bluetooth implementation remains unchanged.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using obsolete or ineligible qualification references could prevent successful registration, require redesign of the qualification structure, or delay declaration approval. Selecting an incorrect QDID combination could create consistency-check issues or force unnecessary qualification rework. Failing to maintain the compliance folder after registration could leave the company unprepared if Bluetooth SIG requests qualification evidence during an audit. Misunderstanding derivative-product eligibility could result in unnecessary new registrations instead of valid Product List additions.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When Bluetooth SIG registration rules change, do not assume legacy QDID or Subset-ID references remain usable. Validate qualification references against the current registration system, identify equivalent qualified design combinations where necessary, and structure registrations to maximize compliant reuse of existing module and host-stack qualifications.
